compiler: Local ptxas/nvdisasm CUDA 12.9.86 for static sm_89 register+SASS analysis only; no GPU and no timed run on this host. Official Yukon build for RTX 4090 is authoritative.
note: Baseline 0b2c7b0 / ff275e40. The only change is the second argument of __launch_bounds__ on kernel_pinning_pipeline<true,2> (the finish kernel): QSB_S2_BLOCKS 7 -> 8. ptxas re-allocates that kernel from 70 registers at 7 resident blocks/SM to 62 registers at 8 blocks/SM with zero spill stores and zero spill loads, emitting the same 3888 SASS instructions (verified by disassembling both builds and diffing the opcode sequence: identical count, minor scheduling reorder only). Occupancy goes 28 -> 32 warps/SM; the kernel uses 0 bytes of shared memory so nothing else caps the eighth block. QSB_S2_BLOCKS has exactly one use, the launch-bounds directive, so candidate enumeration, recovery arithmetic, hit logic and emitted records are untouched. Every other kernel's register/spill profile is byte-for-byte unchanged. The prepare kernel's analogous 4->5 block step was measured and deliberately NOT taken here: it costs 16 B of spill and a 2.6% larger instruction stream, so it is a real trade rather than a free one. This host has no GPU, so there is no local throughput measurement; speed is left to Yukon's authoritative build and benchmark.
